subject: mathematics
question_text: If 4i + (2p/3)j + pk is parallel to the vector i + 2j + 3k, find p.

mark_split.label: State the condition for parallel vectors
Equate the ratios of like components
Check the value in every component

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.71, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 20. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the condition, the ratio statement, the value of p, and the substitution back — the last mark is deliberate because the middle ratio (2p/3)/2 simplifies to p/3 and therefore adds no new information, and a student who never checks it cannot know that. ANSWER IS DETERMINATE: p = 12. VERIFIED by substitution — with p = 12 the vector is 4i + 8j + 12k = 4(i + 2j + 3k), an exact scalar multiple, and the cross product test gives (4, 8, 12) × (1, 2, 3) = i(24 − 24) − j(12 − 12) + k(8 − 8) = 0, the zero vector, which is the parallel condition written the other way. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find p — say what being parallel tells you about the components.

steps.label: State the condition for parallel vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Parallel means one vector is a fixed multiple of the other, so every pair of like components carries the same multiplier.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel means one is a multiple of the other, so like components share one common ratio.
lines: a is parallel to b ⇒ a = t b, t ≠ 0.
So like components are in one ratio.

recall.must_convey: That parallel vectors satisfy a = t b, so the ratios of like components are all equal.
accept: parallel means a equals some scalar t times b
so the like components are in the same ratio
one vector is a constant multiple of the other
parallel ante okati inkoka dani multiple
write a as t times b
reject: use a dot b equals zero

steps.why: Parallel vectors lie along the same line, so one must be a fixed multiple of the other. Component by component that multiple is the same number, which is why the ratios are equal.
common_mistakes: Using the perpendicular condition a·b = 0 instead.
Pairing the i component of one vector with the j component of the other.

steps.label: Equate the ratios of like components
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write all three ratios before solving. The middle one simplifies to p/3, the same as the third, so it decides nothing on its own.
steps.memory_tip: Write all three ratios first — here the middle one repeats the third, so it adds no new equation.

recall.must_convey: That the three ratios are 4/1, (2p/3)/2 and p/3, and the middle one simplifies to p/3.
accept: four over one equals two p by three over two equals p over three
the middle ratio simplifies to p over three
write all three ratios of like components

the second and third ratios are the same expression

steps.why: Writing all three ratios shows which of them actually fixes p. Here the middle ratio reduces to p/3, so the first and third are the pair that determine the value.
common_mistakes: Turning one ratio upside down, for example writing 1/4.

steps.label: Solve for p
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The first and third ratios give 4 = p/3 at once. Cross multiply rather than cancelling terms.
steps.memory_tip: Use the two ratios that carry plain numbers, 4/1 and p/3, and cross multiply.

recall.must_convey: That 4/1 = p/3 gives p = 12, and that 2p/3 is then 8, whose ratio to 2 is also 4.
accept: four equals p over three so p is twelve
cross multiply to get p equal to twelve
then two p by three is eight and eight over two is four
p equals twelve, cross multiply chesthe vastundi
the value of p is twelve

steps.why: The first and third ratios contain only numbers and p, so they give the value directly. The middle ratio is then used as a check, not as a second equation.
common_mistakes: Dividing instead of cross multiplying, giving p = 4/3.

steps.label: Check the value in every component
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Substitute p = 12 back: the vector becomes exactly 4 times b, and the cross product is the zero vector, which is the same test written another way.
steps.memory_tip: Substitute the value back and look for an exact multiple — the cross product is then the zero vector.
lines: Both tests confirm a is parallel to b.

recall.must_convey: That p = 12 makes the vector 4(i + 2j + 3k), an exact multiple of b, and that a × b is then the zero vector.
accept: substituting twelve gives four times i plus two j plus three k
so a is four times b and the cross product is zero
the answer is p equals twelve
p twelve pettinappudu a equals four b avutundi
check by substitution, a cross b is the zero vector
reject: parallel means one is a multiple

steps.why: Substituting the value back shows the first vector is exactly 4 times the second, so they really are parallel. A cross product of the zero vector is the same statement in another form, and it also checks the middle component.
common_mistakes: Stopping at p = 12 without testing the middle component.
Saying the two vectors are equal rather than parallel.
